name: Inverse
tagline: The withdrawal button (§ 356a BGB) and the cancellation button (§ 312k BGB) for Next.js and React, with the two-step flow, the receipt e-mail and a page check.
seoTitle: Inverse – Widerrufsbutton and Kündigungsbutton for Next.js and React
description:
Since 19 June 2026, every online business that concludes contracts with consumers in the EU needs a withdrawal button labelled "Vertrag widerrufen". German subscription businesses have needed a cancellation button labelled "Verträge hier kündigen" since 2022. Shopify, Shopware and WooCommerce have plugins for this; custom shops, SaaS products and booking apps built with Next.js or React mostly don't.

Inverse adds both buttons to your own app. It gets the details right that courts look at: the statutory labels, a second step with "Widerruf bestätigen" or "Jetzt kündigen", the time of receipt set by your server, an acknowledgement e-mail with the content of the declaration, and a copy the consumer can download. You keep the data and send the e-mail with your own provider. A CLI checks your pages for the buttons, so a redesign can't quietly remove them.

faq.a: The withdrawal button is needed wherever consumers can conclude a contract on your site or app, including shops, bookings and subscriptions. The cancellation button is needed in Germany for continuing contracts such as subscriptions and memberships that can be concluded online. Many SaaS products need both.

faq.q: Does Inverse store anything or send data to you?
faq.a: No. The handler calls your own function to store the declaration and your own mail provider to send the receipt. Nothing goes to Inverse or to us.
Yes, every text can be overridden. The law allows an equivalent, unambiguous wording, but the statutory labels are the safe choice, so they are the default.

Yes. The handler takes a Fetch API Request and returns a Response, so it runs on Remix, Hono, SvelteKit, Astro and any Node server. The forms need React; without React you can render your own and post to the same handler.
No. Inverse implements the published wording and process of § 356a and § 312k BGB and explains its reasoning in the docs. For your specific case, ask a lawyer or your trade association.
